meta.marketMethod: Close, prior close and traded volume are read from NSE EQ rows; changePct=(close/previous close-1)*100; avg20VolumeShares is the arithmetic mean of the prior 20 available EQ sessions.
meta.historicalDisclosure: Issuer results signals and Pull briefs are from FY25 publications dated Apr–May 2025. Their dates are preserved and are not presented as Nov 2026 news.
meta.researchMethod: Pull briefs link only issuer annual reports and management earnings-call transcripts. Historical Push result signals use issuer results releases; no broker notes or news sources are used.

signals.title: FY25 revenue +7.1%; EBITDA and PAT each +2.9%
signals.summary: Consolidated revenue grew 7.1% to ₹10,71,174 crore; EBITDA and PAT each rose 2.9%. The Board recommended a ₹5.50/share dividend.
signals.whatChanged: FY25 revenue growth outpaced EBITDA and PAT growth; the Board recommended a ₹5.50/share dividend.
signals.whyItMatters: The earnings mix is a more restrained signal than the top-line growth headline; segment trends matter for the next read-through.
signals.whatToVerify: Compare the next quarter's O2C, Digital Services and Retail operating updates with this consolidated picture.

source.excerpt: Record Annual Consolidated Revenue at ₹1,071,174 crore ($125.3 billion), up 7.1% Y-o-Y.

signals.title: Q4 consolidated PAT ₹188.3bn; FY25 PAT ₹707.9bn
signals.summary: HDFC Bank reported consolidated Q4 PAT of ₹188.3bn and FY25 PAT of ₹707.9bn. The release also reports standalone Q4 net revenue of ₹440.9bn and NII of ₹320.7bn, up 10.3% YoY.
signals.whatChanged: The FY25 release gives separate consolidated and standalone views; standalone Q4 NII grew 10.3% YoY.
signals.whyItMatters: The merger makes like-for-like comparisons delicate; the release notes prior-year standalone revenue included a subsidiary stake-sale gain.
signals.whatToVerify: Keep consolidated and standalone series separate and check the bank's next disclosure for normalized NII and deposit growth.

signals.title: FY25 revenue +3.8%; operating margin 24.3%
signals.summary: TCS reported FY25 revenue of US$30.18bn, up 3.8% YoY; operating margin was 24.3%, net margin 19.0%, and FY25 TCV was US$39.4bn.
signals.whatChanged: FY25 revenue growth was 3.8%; the company also reported US$39.4bn of total contract value for the year.
signals.whyItMatters: TCV is a forward work indicator, while revenue growth shows realized conversion; the gap is worth tracking alongside margin.
signals.whatToVerify: Compare the next constant-currency revenue update and operating margin with the reported TCV conversion.

briefs.name: Bajaj Finance
briefs.basis: Company-reported annual figures; not a live estimate
briefs.businessSnapshot: Consumer, MSME, commercial and rural financial services; the annual report describes a diversified lending and customer-acquisition model.
briefs.thesis: FY25 growth stayed strong across AUM, income and profit, while the sharp rise in loan-loss provisions makes unsecured-credit quality the central counter-signal.

metrics.label: Additional ECL model provision
metrics.basis: Management-reported; included in the credit-cost line per the call

briefs.narrativeVsNumbers: AUM grew 26% and PAT 16% for FY25, but loan-loss provisions rose 72%. In Q4, management separately identified an additional ₹359 crore ECL provision and a ₹348 crore tax reduction; reported Q4 PAT growth therefore needs those one-offs in view.

bull.claim: FY25 AUM grew 26%, net total income 24%, and PAT 16%; the customer franchise reached 101.82 million.

bear.claim: Loan-loss provisions increased 72%; management cited macro deterioration, leverage in unsecured loans and rising banking-sector stress.

evidence.claim: AUM increased 26% to ₹416,661 crore in FY25.
evidence.excerpt: The shareholder letter reports FY25 AUM of ₹416,661 crore, up 26% year over year.

evidence.claim: Loan-loss provisions rose 72% to ₹7,966 crore; the letter cites macro deterioration, unsecured leverage and banking-sector stress.
evidence.excerpt: The letter links higher provisions to macro conditions, unsecured leverage and banking-sector stress.

evidence.claim: Management reported Q4 PBT growth of 11% and PAT growth of 19%, alongside additional ECL provision and lower tax expense.
evidence.pageOrSection: Opening financial highlights and one-off provisions, p. 2
evidence.excerpt: The call separates a ₹359 crore additional ECL provision from a ₹348 crore tax expense reduction.

briefs.name: Titan Company
briefs.basis: Audited consolidated figures unless noted; ₹ crore
briefs.businessSnapshot: Jewellery is the largest business, with watches and wearables, eyecare, international and newer consumer businesses alongside it.
briefs.thesis: Revenue advanced strongly, but consolidated PBT and PAT declined; the annual report’s standalone jewellery discussion notes gold-price and customs-duty effects, while management described pressure at lower jewellery price points.

metrics.label: EBITDA-equivalent line item
metrics.basis: Consolidated; issuer line item is profit before exceptional items, finance costs, depreciation and taxes

briefs.narrativeVsNumbers: Management described the Q4 performance as satisfying despite gold-rate and discretionary-consumption pressure, and targeted high-double-digit jewellery growth. FY25 consolidated revenue grew 18.4%, but PBT fell 1.9% and PAT 4.6%; the annual report’s standalone jewellery discussion notes gold-price and customs-duty effects.

bull.claim: FY25 consolidated revenue rose 18.4%; the issuer EBITDA-equivalent line item rose 6.1%, while consolidated PBT fell 1.9% and PAT fell 4.6%. Standalone jewellery revenue excluding bullion was ₹46,571 crore.
bull.pageOrSection: Consolidated Financial Results, printed p. 119 (PDF p. 121); standalone jewellery division, printed p. 120 (PDF p. 122)

bull.claim: Management continued to target high-double-digit jewellery growth.
bull.pageOrSection: Jewellery margin and growth outlook, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 6)

bear.claim: Consolidated PBT fell 1.9% and PAT fell 4.6% in FY25.
bear.pageOrSection: Consolidated Financial Results, printed p. 119 (PDF p. 121)

bear.claim: Management described pressure in lower jewellery price bands amid gold-price uncertainty.
bear.pageOrSection: Lower-price band commentary, printed pp. 2-3 (PDF pp. 3-4)

evidence.claim: Consolidated FY25 revenue was ₹60,456 crore; PBT was ₹4,535 crore and profit for the year ₹3,337 crore.
evidence.pageOrSection: Financial Results table, printed p. 119 (PDF p. 121)
evidence.excerpt: The audited consolidated results table reports revenue of ₹60,456 crore, PBT of ₹4,535 crore and profit of ₹3,337 crore.

evidence.claim: Standalone jewellery division revenue, excluding bullion sales, was ₹46,571 crore, up 21%.
evidence.pageOrSection: Standalone jewellery division, printed p. 120 (PDF p. 122)
evidence.excerpt: The report presents jewellery revenue separately from bullion sales and reports 21% growth.

evidence.claim: Management held its jewellery margin outlook at 11%-11.5%.
evidence.pageOrSection: Jewellery margin outlook, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 6)
evidence.excerpt: Management described the 11%-11.5% jewellery margin range as a more reasonable outlook amid uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Management described pressure in lower jewellery price bands amid gold-price uncertainty.
evidence.pageOrSection: Lower-price band commentary, printed pp. 2-3 (PDF pp. 3-4)
evidence.excerpt: Management described pressure in lower price bands under uncertainty in gold prices.

Jewellery EBIT margin versus the 11%-11.5% range discussed on the call
